messages:
Alex: Heads-up — after enabling per-layer 4-bit quant (exclude embed+lm_head) we see a tail-latency regression for cached requests on p3x2s.
Alex: Short repro: stable throughput for cold requests, but cached prefix requests 95p latency doubled.
Alex: Profiling snippet I ran locally:
```
$ ./tools/profile_run --model my-model --quant per-layer4 --exclude embed,lm_head --seq 512 --warm 200 --it 1000
KV cache hit reqs: 82%  | avg latency: 58ms | p95: 210ms
Kernel selector: selected int4_kv_kernel -> fallback to fp8_kv_kernel on 12% calls
hot_kernel_switches: 154
```
Mira: :thinking: fallback to fp8_kv_kernel on cached calls — that suggests we’re hitting a codepath mismatch when filling KV with quantized tensors. Any blind promotions happening at runtime?
Sam: I saw this once — our kernel-selector picks int4 for attention but the KV packer still emits fp16 strides when a layer has mixed-precision params (e.g., Q at int4, K/V at fp8). That forces memcpy + conversion -> tail hit.
Mira: Could also be batching heuristic. If batching collapses cached prefixes into bigger micro-batches, the warmup sequence for the fallback kernel gets triggered more often.
Jordan: Proposal: change dynamic batch heuristic to consider (active_kv_bytes, selected_kernel) so we avoid forcing large batches when KV layout causes slow conversions.
Jordan: Example config change:
```
batching:
  max_tokens: 4096
  kv_sensitive_threshold_bytes: 1e7
  avoid_mixing_kernels: true
```
Lee: I'll run a per-layer sensitivity scan to see which layers trigger layout promotions. Running: `scripts/scan_layer_sensitivity --quant int4 --check-kv-layout --out /tmp/sens.json`
Lee: If we can map offending layers, we can add per-layer override to keep K/V in fp16 for those layers while Q is int4.
Alex: That would be a partial-quant strategy: keep embeddings & lm_head excluded (we already do), + selective K/V exclusion for sensitive layers.
Sam: Quick numbers from a tiny run (seq=256, batch=8):
- all-int4 (excluded embed/lm): avg 42ms, p95 120ms
- selective-KV-fp16 on layers 8-11: avg 35ms, p95 78ms
So selective KVFP16 helps a lot for cached tails.
Mira: Sounds promising. Two action items: (1) Lee produces sensitivity map, (2) Jordan prototypes batching change and a selector flag `prefer_stable_kv_layout`.
Jordan: I'll also add telemetry to kernel-selector to surface how often fallback occurs per route/model.
DeployBot: Canary queued: `canary/per-layer-quant-selective-kv-202603` — will run on 5% infra in us-west for 3 hours.
Alex: Thanks. If canary looks good, we should roll to 25% and run the same perf monitors (p50/p95/p99 on cached prefixes + kernel-fallback counts).
Lee: Starting scan now, ETA ~45m. Will post results here (sens map + layer list).
Sam: FYI, if we add per-layer KV exclusions, we should add a simple cost-estimator in Optimize to show token-cost delta.
Mira: Agreed. Also add a quick unit test to catch accidental layout promotion in the kernel-selector.
Alex: Great. I'll create the follow-up GH issues: outline, benchmarks to run, and assign people. :thumbsup:
